handbookNote: Priced at $0.99 (2026-08-16 directive): TX's education requirement (SB 693) is real, but no confirmed graded assessment exists (see status note below), so this is education-only practice content, not exam prep -- priced accordingly, well below the $9.99 exam-state tier. Texas Government Code Chapter 406 (Notary Public; Commissioner of Deeds), Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapter 121 (Acknowledgments and Proofs), and Texas Government Code Chapter 603 (fee-book/posting duties) -- price matches this project's established Notary tier ($9.99), not a placeholder. IMPORTANT STATUS NOTE on the Jan. 1, 2026 education requirement (S.B. 693, Acts 2025, 89th Leg., R.S., Ch. 298): the underlying statute is fully enacted and confirmed -- it added a mandatory notary-education element to Sec. 406.006/406.011/406.023(d) (capped at 2 hours, offered only by the secretary of state, prospective-only as of applications submitted on/after Jan. 1, 2026) -- and this bank is grounded in that enacted text. What could NOT be confirmed as of this track's build date: whether the secretary of state's implementing rule (1 TAC Chapter 87) has been finalized in the Texas Administrative Code (the historical TAC reader now redirects to a new Appian-based portal that would not finish loading even in a live browser session), and whether a specifically named 'Notary Education Assessment' with a published passing score exists -- that exact phrase/figure appears nowhere in the enacted statute or on the Secretary of State's own site as fetched. No question in this bank is written about assessment specifics for that reason; revisit this note (and 1 TAC Ch. 87) before the next content refresh.
